eligibility.exact_action_basis: The whole MAPWaters House text would require Interior and Agriculture to adopt interagency compatibility/interoperability standards within30months, coordinated with the named Federal Geographic Data Committee. The Act separately defines Federal waterways as waters managed by one or more of the relevant Secretaries, and Federal land/water management agencies as the five named agencies—Reclamation, National Park Service, BLM, Fish and Wildlife Service and Forest Service. The Secretaries would provide online GIS information within five years, to the maximum extent practicable and as applicable, on existing waterway restrictions, access/navigation and fishing restrictions. Waterway restrictions are those applied under applicable law by the relevant Secretaries; the separate fishing-restriction definition concerns the listed agencies, and the boat-ramp/portage/fishing-access-site clause concerns sites under an agency’s authority. Bathymetry/depth charts remain as feasible. Public questions/comments concern section4(a)/(b), not the separate fishing subsection; access/restriction updates are at least twice yearly, fishing updates as changes take effect, subject to practicability. Section4 excludes irrigation canals/flowage easements and protects historic, paleontological and archaeological resource information from disclosure. Optional partners/third parties and USGS assistance, compliance with Federal/State/Tribal law and an applicable-law notice, practicable reuse of existing maps/data, and progress reports starting within one year and annually through March30,2034 remain. Section7 preserves the navigable-waters definition, regulatory/fisheries authority and existing accessibility. This is a qualified information-system duty, not new access rights, new fishing restrictions or construction.

The whole House text would replace2025 with2030 in16USC8102(e) and fix a comma in the Secretary definition. Against the retained2024 baseline, this extends the unchanged $12million annual authorization from fiscal2021–2025 to2021–2030; it does not appropriate funds or award grants. Existing discretionary, need/impacted-area-based State assistance covers nutria eradication/control and restoration of marshland, public/private wetlands and agricultural lands. The baseline's Maryland-specific management/research/public-education provisions reference the named March2002 strategy; they are not a new nationwide research mandate. The75percent federal-share ceiling, in-kind nonfederal contributions and5percent administrative cap remain unchanged.

The whole House text would redesignate Salem Maritime National Historic Site as Salem Maritime National Historical Park and conform federal references. It would require an Interior suitability/feasibility study of possible boundary additions in Salem and its vicinity, including the Salem Armory Visitor Center building and adjacent Armory Park, with the specified maritime, coastal-defense, military and National Guard/militia history considerations. The report is due three years after funds are made available for the study, not three years after enactment. A study of possible additions does not itself expand boundaries, acquire land, authorize construction or appropriate study funding.

The whole House text would establish the named Great Lakes Mass Marking Program in Fish and Wildlife Service statute to assess hatchery/management effectiveness and support Great Lakes fisheries. Its findings describe earlier operations beginning2010, so this is not a claim of first-ever operational creation. The Director may purchase capital/expendable equipment and tags, support tag recovery/data processing/dissemination and hire personnel. Collaboration with applicable federal, State and Tribal fish-management agencies, the Council of Lake Committees and named Joint Strategic Plan signatories is mandatory. Program data must be made available to the specified fish-management agencies for the five printed management/restoration/evaluation purposes, not universally published to everyone. It authorizes $2.7million per fiscal year2026–2030; it does not appropriate that amount or establish actual tagging, habitat or economic results. Numerical findings are legislative assertions rather than independent outcome evidence.

The whole nine-section House text would change several dated water-program authorizations and conditions. Against2024 baselines: Great Lakes Restoration Initiative's $475million for FY2026 becomes that amount for each FY2026–2031; Long Island Sound's $40million FY2019–2023 becomes2019–2031; Columbia's $30million for2020 and2021 becomes2020 through2031; National Estuary Program's $50million FY2022–2026 becomes2022–2031, leaving earlier years/amounts intact; and coastal monitoring's $30million FY2001–2005 becomes FY2026–2031. These authorize appropriations and do not spend money. San Francisco Bay would gain broader agreement/contract/funding mechanisms and Federal/private recipients, replace its entity/year aggregate cap with a75percent per-project/activity/study cap, and require at least25percent nonfederal sources only for assistance to nonfederal entities. The existing5percent administrative cap remains. Mississippi Sound would receive priority consideration for an estuary management conference, not automatic admission. FY2026 NEP funds cannot implement that addition; FY2027 NEP funds also cannot implement that addition unless total FY2027 NEP appropriations are at least FY2024 plus $850000. State/local coastal grants may identify contamination sources; States using that option report associated data, and EPA guidance must reflect testing innovations. Existing conditions for local grants where a State does not implement a program remain. The marine-State designated-contact-recreation definition branch would expressly include river/stream mouths, nearby shallow waters and beach waters; the separate Great Lakes branch and inland/upstream exclusions remain. BEACHES Act section8 would extend its residual such-sums-as-necessary authorization from FY2001–2005 to2026–2031, not create another fixed-dollar pot. For the six enumerated CWA sections118/119/123/125/320/406, Federal funds made available for FY2026–2031 may not be provided to any nonfederal entity domiciled in, headquartered in, organized under the laws of, or with its principal place of business in a foreign country of concern; OR to any nonfederal entity for projects conducted with a foreign country of concern. These are alternative recipient-status or project conditions, using the retained42USC19237(2) definition. The restriction is not a bar on every recipient or all eleven report programs. A GAO report within two years evaluates the eleven listed geographic programs' management, funds, progress, coordination and ethics and recommends improvements; that evaluation is not an adverse finding or a funding change for every listed program. Existing GLRI restrictions on specified water-infrastructure assistance and the green-infrastructure habitat/ecosystem exception remain material: this mixed package is not a universal water-construction grant.

source_render_constraints.detail: All five whole choices held pending independent preparation review and separate content-bound eligibility/meaning decisions. Three new binding proposals unapproved. No canonical application or propositions.
